About the lab

Learning first. Technology with purpose.

The Digital Learning Lab studies how people learn with digital media and builds tools and resources that make those experiences more meaningful, equitable, and effective.

Our story

A lab built around better questions.

The Digital Learning Lab was founded by Mark Warschauer to use cutting-edge approaches for better understanding students’ learning processes, from preschool to graduate school, and to design new tools and resources that improve digital learning opportunities.

Digital media continue to transform learning in higher education and K–12 schools. They also expand the amount and kinds of data available for studying teaching and learning. Our work brings these possibilities together with a clear focus on learners, educators, and communities.

How we work

Research is part of an ecosystem.

01

Understand learning

Study how learners engage, communicate, create, and develop knowledge in digital environments.

02

Design with purpose

Develop platforms and learning experiences around clear educational goals rather than technology alone.

03

Work together

Collaborate with educators, students, schools, institutions, researchers, and community partners.

Across contexts

From early childhood to higher education.

Our projects span science, social studies, language and literacy, early learning, computer science, writing, artificial intelligence, and educator development.

That breadth lets ideas and evidence travel between fields while each project remains grounded in the people and learning context it serves.
